one_liner: Andrew Holme's GPU_FFT: power-of-two complex FFTs on the Raspberry Pi VideoCore IV GPU, about 10x FFTW on the Pi 1 ARM.
what_it_does: GPU_FFT runs single-precision complex FFTs of length 2^8 to 2^22 on the QPU shader cores of the BCM2835-family 3D block (the code launches 8 QPU programs per transform), with a GPU transpose helper for 2D transforms. The C API is three calls: gpu_fft_prepare(mailbox_fd, log2_N, direction, jobs, &fft), gpu_fft_execute(fft) and gpu_fft_release(fft); you write input into fft->in + j*fft->step and read from fft->out. It is not FFTW-compatible: no plans, no strides, no real or odd-length transforms, and the output is not scaled.
how_it_is_fast: Hand-written VideoCore IV QPU assembly (qasm/*.qasm, assembled to hex/*.hex and embedded) splits each transform into a few passes of radix-16, radix-32 or radix-64 butterflies (e.g. the 256-point kernel is two radix-16 passes, the 4M-point kernel two radix-64 passes plus radix-32 passes), loading the first pass bit-reversed and ping-ponging between two buffers, with writes through the VPM and VC4 L2 cache. Twiddles are advanced with a trig recurrence corrected by float-float (df64) subtraction to recover accuracy. For short batches the ARM pokes V3D registers directly and busy-waits instead of using the firmware mailbox, which removes about 100 us of overhead per call.
when_to_use: Spectrum analysis, SDR or audio DSP on a Raspberry Pi 1, Zero or other VideoCore IV board where the ARM core is the bottleneck: the doc table shows 2.8x at 256 points and 8-12x from 4K to 4M points over FFTW_MEASURE on a 700 MHz Pi 1
Many same-size power-of-two transforms that can be batched into one execute call (batch of 10 roughly halves per-transform time at 256-512 points)
Applications that tolerate single precision with 0.33-1.5 ppm rms error
Freeing the ARM CPU for other work while the GPU computes longer transforms (mailbox path for long jobs avoids 100% CPU busy-waiting)
when_not_to_use: Any non-VideoCore IV hardware: the kernels are QPU machine code and gpu_fft_base.c only has Pi 1 and 'Pi 2?' memory paths; support for Pi 4/5 is not documented
Double precision, non-power-of-two lengths, real-input (r2c) transforms or lengths below 256 or above 4,194,304
When accuracy matters: the doc says FFTW is still one order of magnitude more accurate
Programs that cannot run as root: mailbox.c opens /dev/mem and /dev/vcio and maps the V3D registers
New projects on current Raspberry Pi OS: the userland repo README calls itself ancient and deprecated, the repo is archived, and its code is no longer installed on Bookworm images

integration.dependencies: Raspberry Pi firmware mailbox device (/dev/vcio), /dev/mem, libbcm_host.so (dlopen'd for SDRAM and peripheral addresses), librt, libm, libdl
integration.min_toolchain: Plain C (gcc, no flags in the makefile); prebuilt shader hex files included, the QPU assembler is only needed to change kernels
integration.platforms: Raspberry Pi boards with the VideoCore IV GPU (BCM2835 Pi 1/Zero; gpu_fft_base.c also has a Pi 2 memory path); 32-bit Raspbian/Raspberry Pi OS era firmware
integration.thread_safety: not documented; one process owns the V3D block per execute call, and on Pi 1 OpenGL can share it only with GPU_FFT_USE_VC4_L2_CACHE set to 0 and explicit glFinish() between uses

gotchas: Input is destroyed and the result is out of place for log2_N 12-16 (odd pass count) but in place otherwise; always read fft->out.
GPU memory is permanently lost until reboot if gpu_fft_release() is not called (doc and hello_fft.c comment), so crash handling matters.
The direct-register path (batches up to about 1 ms of work) busy-waits on V3D_SRQCS with no timeout; only the mailbox path has the 2000 ms timeout.
Buffers are separated by fft->step, which is larger than N because of guard space; index batches with step, not N.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick GPU_FFT itself when you can change the code and want the full speed, batching and the 2D transpose; gpu_fftw (already catalogued) is an LD_PRELOAD shim over this same library that keeps the FFTW API but copies arrays, falls back to FFTW and supports only 1-D 2^8-2^21. On anything other than a VideoCore IV Pi, the CPU libraries in the list (FFTW itself, PocketFFT, PFFFT, Ne10 on ARM) are the options.
verified_claims_summary: The library author's own gpu_fft.txt (release 3.0, 2015) gives per-transform times on a 700 MHz Pi 1 with VC4 L2 cache enabled: GPU_FFT at batch 1 takes 0.033 ms vs 0.092 ms for FFTW_MEASURE at 256 points, 0.25 vs 3.0 ms at 4K, 7.0 vs 83 ms at 64K and 786 vs 8800 ms at 4M (2.8x to 12x). The FFTW version, build flags and timing code are not published; hello_fft.c only times the GPU side with clock_gettime and reports rms error.
status_note: Abandoned: last hello_fft commit 2022-06-16 and raspberrypi/userland archived on 2025-08-27 with a README telling users to rethink solutions built on it; BSD-3-Clause and only a handful of C files plus shader hex, so it is easy to vendor for legacy Pi 1/Zero projects.
